claims.evidence_span: However, the strength of single phase type HEAs were reported to be insufficient at elevated temperatures
the development for precipitation strengthened HEAs is only at the incipient stage, and more research efforts will be required

claims.content: Low matrix stacking-fault energy, high precipitate APB energy, and microstructural stability strengthen HESA.
claims.evidence_span: HESA could be strengthened by the low stacking-fault energy of the matrix, high anti-phase boundary energy of the strengthening precipitate, and thermally stable microstructure

claims.content: Positive lattice misfit produces parallel rafts during creep.
claims.evidence_span: Positive misfit between FCC matrix and precipitate has yielded parallel raft microstructure during creep at 982 °C
the reduction of SFE due to alloying for CMSX-2 is 0.4 J/m 2 , while that for HESA should be 0.6 J/m 2

claims.content: HESA creep rupture life rivals first-generation superalloys.
claims.evidence_span: The creep rupture life of HESA at 982 °C is about 114 h, which is similar to those of several first-generation Ni-based superalloys

claims.content: HESA creep is dominated by tertiary deformation.
claims.evidence_span: the creep curves of HESA were dominated by tertiary creep behavior

claims.content: Parallel rafting removes perpendicular gamma/gamma-prime interfaces during creep.
claims.evidence_span: the creep of HESA is dominated by parallel raft (P-raft) and without perpendicular γ/γ′ interfaces

claims.content: Prior studies inferred HEA creep mechanisms with nanoindentation.
claims.evidence_span: some studies utilized nano-indentation method to deduce creep mechanism of HEA

claims.content: Nanoindentation cannot include long-term microstructural stability.
claims.evidence_span: these tests could not take the effect of long-term microstructure stability on creep into consideration

claims.content: Earlier gamma-prime HEAs had lower solvus temperatures than conventional superalloys.
claims.evidence_span: the γ′ solvus temperatures of the reported γ′-bearing HEAs still remained relatively low comparing to those of superalloys

claims.content: HESA has a 1199 degrees C gamma-prime solvus and 69% precipitate fraction.
claims.evidence_span: the γ′ solvus and solidus temperature are 1199 and 1276 °C, respectively

claims.content: HESA creep activation energy is 290 kJ/mol versus 230 kJ/mol for CMSX-2.
claims.evidence_span: the creep activation energy of HESA can be estimated to be 290 kJ/mol, while that of CMSX-2 is 230 kJ/mol

claims.content: Dislocations bypass rather than shear gamma-prime precipitates during creep.
claims.evidence_span: Instead, thermally activated by-passing of dislocations around γ′ precipitates should be the deformation mechanism

claims.content: Parallel rafting explains the observed dominance of tertiary creep.
claims.evidence_span: Tetzlaff et al . have reported that tertiary creep may dominate the creep response of P-rafted superalloys [47] , and this is exactly the creep behavior observed for HESA at 982 °C

claims.content: Sluggish diffusion in the high-entropy matrix raises creep activation energy.
claims.evidence_span: the sluggish diffusion of the high entropy γ matrix may have attributed to the higher creep activation energy
